findings.title: Serialize index creation per namespaced resource
findings.body: The cache lock now protects only publication, so GetIndex returns nil while an index is being built. Concurrent searches, or a search and the write-event handler, can consequently build separate indexes for the same key. If the event handler publishes its index and applies an update before the other build publishes an older snapshot, that second publication discards the update and leaves searches permanently stale until another event or restart. File-backed builds also compete to create the same directory and can fail. Keep builds parallel across different keys, but coordinate creation and publication for each individual key.

findings.title: Protect TotalDocs against concurrent cache publication
findings.body: This new TotalDocs call runs after the search write-event listener has started. That listener can build and publish an index for a resource omitted from startup indexing (for example, one below InitMinCount). bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates its cache map without taking cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes that map under the mutex. An event arriving during this startup log can therefore cause a data race or a fatal concurrent-map-iteration-and-write crash. Add read locking to TotalDocs before invoking it concurrently with index creation.
